# gatekeep-pr 642: obstacle pick `2`, then assess terminal

## 0. Recover the run record

1. Read the existing `state: <absolute-path>` record named in the first tracker task. Nothing is minted, discovered or inferred from chat.
2. Validate the record before any write:
   - `consent.target` matches the lowercased base repository `meadow/events`, PR number `642`, and `baseRefName` `main`.
   - Stored head `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111` and body match.
   - The stored scope baseline is unchanged: `source: pr`, no rows, `original_intent: reject unsigned events`.
3. The recovered values are course `deliver`, `rounds_used 1/rounds_cap 6`, `syncs_used 1/syncs_cap 6`.
4. No in-flight wave stage needs reconciliation. The record is valid, so no `stuck - run record unreadable` exit applies.

## 1. Take the numeric pick `2`

1. Apply menu-layout. The obstacle menu followed the prose `Pick one:` line, so `L = 0` and `N = 3`. Reply `2` maps directly to row 2, `assess`, with no echo.
2. Per `### Continuation record`, an obstacle `assess` pick switches the course from deliver to assess.
3. Persist `course: assess` before any course-authorized write. Usage counters stay at 1/6 and 1/6 and are not reset.
4. Assess authorizes no repair and no sync.

## 2. Take `show evidence`

This is an exact typed command, recognized before numeric lookup. It prints the record per `report.md` `## What stays out`:
- `state: <absolute-path>`
- course `assess`
- target `meadow/events#642 -> main`
- scope baseline
- usage `rounds 1/6, syncs 1/6`
- deadline and wave checkpoints, and failed-prerequisite history
- CI evidence: `ci / test`, success, `1111111`, `https://git.example.invalid/meadow/events/actions/runs/910`
- claim dispositions
- check dispositions
- drafted payloads

It settles nothing and does not revoke the persisted assess pick.

## 3. Boundary refresh

This runs at the Next-action boundary. It is also the pre-menu refresh, and the compare-and-swap before the external write.

1. `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit`
2. `gh run list -R meadow/events -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`

Results:
- Head unchanged at `1111111…`.
- Body unchanged.
- `baseRefName` is `main`, matching `consent.target`.
- State is OPEN.
- `mergeable: CONFLICTING`.
- `ci / test` is still success on run 910.
- The refreshed state carries a source-backed `P1`: the guard accepts an event with an empty signature.

Because the head is unchanged, the run re-enters step 5. The tracker adds `report` now; `menu` is added when step 6 starts.

Under course assess, CONFLICTING triggers no Loop sync and the blocker triggers no fix wave. No implementer, no reviewer helper and no push run.

## 4. Assess write (own PR, so `--comment`)

1. **Output done-check.** The review body is:
   - one summary sentence;
   - the numbered blocker with its locator, phrased as the report's blocker sentence;
   - closing on the asked fix.
   
   It passes: ASCII only, no scaffolding, ends on the action.
2. **Compare-and-swap re-fetch.** `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`. The head, body and base are unchanged and the PR is OPEN, so the write proceeds.
3. **Post.** `gh pr review 642 -R meadow/events --comment --body-file <tmp>` returns success. No C# thread replies are posted; there are none.
4. **Render.** The run renders the assess terminal.

Verification and the brief assessed SHA `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`.

**Sync line:** none renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.

## 5. Rendered report and first menu

```
Delivers: the event guard rejects unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. The guard accepts an event whose signature field is empty, so an unsigned event slips past the check. (src/guard.ts)

Verdict: fixable - 1 blocker

Pick one:
1. deliver - switch back to delivery: repair the blocker, rebase on main to clear the conflict, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered.
2. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is. [recommended]

Not offered: approve (your own PR); merge (open blocker; merge conflict with main).
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.
```

The run stops here and awaits the pick.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers all three facts: it validates the supplied record (course deliver, 1/6 and 1/6) rather than rejecting it, maps numeric 2 to the obstacle `assess` row and persists `course: assess` with counters untouched before any write, runs no repair or sync under assess despite the fresh P1 and CONFLICTING, treats `show evidence` as a read-only print that settles nothing, and posts exactly one `gh pr review --comment` on the own PR before rendering the assess terminal with approve omitted. Before fails because it has no course model at all: it declares the record malformed for carrying course/caps/sync fields, refuses `2` as a non-verb, never persists a switch (so the 'after the switch' premise of f2 never exists), discards rather than preserves caps/usage, and posts nothing while re-rendering an old-style fix/update-branch menu. Nothing in After regressed a fact Before kept; the only wording caution is that the Change's new numeric-course handling must keep stating that counters are not reset on a switch and that assess posts one comment review (never request-changes) on an own PR, which After does explicitly in sections 1 and 4 and should be retained verbatim.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps all three facts: the bare `2` is persisted as `course: assess` with rounds 1/6 and syncs 1/6 intact before any refresh or write (f1), the narration explicitly lists no fetch/rebase/merge/test/commit/push and no helper dispatch (f2), and the single own-PR `gh pr review --comment` post plus the explicit 'show evidence does not select delivery, settle the blocker, authorize sync' statement with unchanged counters satisfy f3. Before also held every fact, so nothing moved here; the real differences are structural: After defers `show evidence` until after the assess post and terminal render (Entry orders it right after the `2` pick), re-renders the full terminal menu twice, and references an undeclared `$REVIEW_BODY` where it had introduced only `$STATE`/`$WT`. To stay aligned with the Entry sequence while delivering the shared-menu course model, handle `show evidence` immediately after persisting the course (before the refresh/write), render the assess terminal once, and define the review-body path variable alongside the others.
